doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Lutheran school and music only from home and church
summary: She went to a Lutheran school after a fight at public school, liked drawing letters and music, and had no school music program.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: School yes. I went to a Lutheran school. They wanted me to go to a religious school, but not a Catholic school. In my religion Catholics were sort of mystical, and too weird. So, the Lutherans were a little mystical and weird too, but that’s the school that they put me in, until I guess the sixth grade. Oh no, I went to school for six months at a
regular public school but then I got into a fight with someone, and so they switched me to a Lutheran school.
Was there any, at that particular time, any areas of study that were an interest of yours?
I liked drawing letters. You know, alphabet.
Ok. Science, or any of that?
Ok. Was there, besides your parents, was there a music program in your school that you benefitted from?
So it was really all from home and church?
